name: Pura Meduwe Karang
deity: Batara Meduwe Karang ("lord possessing the ground")
significance: A large north Balinese temple raised in 1890 by villagers who had resettled at Kubutambahan from the abandoned village of Bulian, addressed to the deity who owns the ground and petitioned for the fertility of unirrigated farmland. Its outer terrace carries thirty-six stone figures from the Ramayana and its walls the flowery relief carving typical of the north coast.

name: Pura Pulaki
significance: One of the sea temples set around the coast of Bali to form a protective chain, founded in 1489 by the Majapahit brahmin priest Dang Hyang Nirartha. Left abandoned for centuries, it was leased to a Chinese trader under the Dutch administration in 1920 and restored by the Indonesian government after 1950.
story: Local tradition holds that when Nirartha reached the shore the forest macaques escorted him to the spot where the temple would stand.

name: Pura Beji Sangsit
significance: A subak temple of the Sangsit rice-growing community, dedicated to the rice goddess Dewi Sri and dated to the fifteenth century, when brahmins arrived from the Majapahit kingdom. It takes its name from the beji, the pond used for purification, and is covered in the heavy foliate carving that distinguishes north Balinese work from that of the south.

name: Pura Taman Saraswati
significance: Commissioned by the prince of Ubud, Cokorda Gede Agung Sukawati, and designed by the sculptor and ritual architect I Gusti Nyoman Lempad, the temple was begun in 1951 and finished in 1952. Dedicated to Sarasvati, goddess of learning, literature and art, it is among Ubud's best-known landmarks for the lotus pond and water garden fronting its outer courtyard.

name: Pura Gede Perancak
significance: A sea temple on the Perancak estuary in Jembrana marking the place where the priest Dang Hyang Nirartha is held to have come ashore in Bali in 1546. Once sited on a hilltop and known as Tanjung Ketapang, it was moved to the marshland side and rebuilt twice as a dang kahyangan temple, anchoring the Hindu community in a largely Muslim district.
story: The name is traced to ancak, meaning split: when the village head I Gusti Ngurah challenged Nirartha, the stone seat beneath him is said to have cracked apart.

name: Pura Dalem Segara Madhu
significance: The death temple of Jagaraga in Buleleng, dedicated to Durga and Shiva and thought to have been founded in the twelfth century. Destroyed during the Dutch intervention of 1849, it was rebuilt from 1865 and is known for dense north Balinese wall carving that includes reliefs of early aeroplanes and motor cars.

name: Garuda Wisnu Kencana statue
significance: A 121-metre statue of Vishnu riding the divine bird Garuda, designed by the sculptor Nyoman Nuarta in 1990, begun in 1997 and completed in 2018 after a sixteen-year halt caused by the Asian financial crisis. It is the tallest statue in Indonesia and the tallest depiction of a Hindu deity anywhere.
story: The myth it renders has Garuda agree to carry Vishnu in exchange for the elixir with which he freed his enslaved mother.

name: Pura Penataran Agung Lempuyang
deity: Sang Hyang Widhi and the Trimurti
significance: The first and lowest of the seven temples of the Pura Lempuyang complex, standing about 603 m up the south-western flank of Mount Lempuyang in Karangasem, with Pura Lempuyang Luhur at the summit. Epigraphs record a ruler named Jayacakti being sent to build it in the late tenth century, and worship on this mountain is held to predate most Hindu temples on Bali; the temple was restored in 2001.
